arguments.text: Fixed. Bug: `Interval.fromISO` called `DateTime.fromISO` on both halves of the string, and with `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true` the DateTime parse of a duration half (e.g. `P1Y2M10DT2H30M`) threw an InvalidDateTimeError before the code could fall back to `Duration.fromISO`. Now each half is parsed in a try/catch, recording validity instead of propagating the throw, so `<start>/<duration>` and `<duration>/<end>` forms work with throwOnInvalid and genuinely unparsable input still raises an InvalidIntervalError. Verified: `Interval.fromISO("2007-03-01T13:00:00/2008-05-11T15:30:00")`, `.../P1Y2M10DT2H30M`, and `P1Y2M10DT2H30M/2008-05-11T15:30:00` all return valid Intervals under `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true`. No pre-existing tests broken (the only 2 failures are the pre-existing ICU/locale ones in toFormat.test.js).

Fixed. Bug: in `src/impl/util.js`, `objToLocalTS` corrected years 0–99 by doing `d.setUTCFullYear(d.getUTCFullYear() - 1900)` after the date was already normalized. Since the intermediate year (19xx/2000) can be a leap year while the target year (e.g. 100) is not, dates landing on/after Feb 29 were shifted by a day — so e.g. `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ day: 61 })` returned 0100-03-01 instead of 0100-03-02. It now calls `d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)`, re-applying month/day so normalization happens in the correct year. Cross-checked against an independent proleptic-Gregorian reference over all years 0–99: 0 mismatches (old code had 46). No pre-existing tests broken.

arguments.text: Fixed. Bug: `DateTime#isInDST` decided DST by comparing the current offset only against the offsets in January and May of the same year. In years where DST covers those months — the US in 1974, when DST ran from Jan 6 02:00 to Oct 27 02:00 — both reference offsets were themselves DST, so `isInDST` wrongly returned false for the entire DST period (e.g. Oct 26, 1974 in America/New_York). It now compares the current offset against the smallest offset the zone uses across the twelve months of the year (its standard-time offset) and reports DST when the current offset is greater. Verified: every instant from 1974-01-06T02:00 to 1974-10-27T01:59 in America/New_York is true, and Jan 1–5 / Oct 27 02:00 onward are false; southern-hemisphere (Australia/Sydney), no-DST (Asia/Tokyo, UTC), fixed-offset and invalid cases all still behave correctly. Cross-checked against Intl long time-zone names for 13 zones over 1970–2030: mismatches drop from 263 (old) to 75 (remaining ones are zones whose standard offset changed mid-year, e.g. Alaska 1983). No pre-existing tests broken (only the 2 pre-existing ICU/locale failures remain).

arguments.text: Fixed. Bug: `padStart` in `src/impl/util.js` padded by prepending zeros to the whole stringified number and then slicing, so the minus sign of a negative year was treated as a digit — `padStart(-1, 4)` gave "00-1" and `DateTime.fromObject({ year: -1, month: 5, day: 25 }).toISODate()` gave "00-1-05-25". It now pads the absolute digits and re-attaches the sign, giving "-0001-05-25" (and "-0010-05-25", "-0100-05-25", "-1000-05-25" for -10/-100/-1000), matching ISO 8601 expanded year representation. Positive years, offsets and fractional formatting are unchanged (verified `padStart(1)="01"`, `padStart(100,2)="100"`, `padStart(0.5,4)="00.5"`). Full suite: same 892 passing, only the 2 pre-existing ICU/locale failures remain; eslint clean.

arguments.text: Fixed. Bug: `FixedOffsetZone#isValid` was hard-coded to `true`, so a zone built from a non-numeric offset (e.g. `new FixedOffsetZone("blorp")` or `FixedOffsetZone.instance(undefined)`) claimed to be valid and was accepted by the zone-normalizing code paths. It now returns `isNumber(this.fixed)`, so such zones are invalid and any DateTime created with one is invalid with reason "unsupported zone" (verified across fromObject/fromMillis/fromJSDate/fromISO/fromRFC2822/fromSQL/fromHTTP/fromFormat/setZone). Valid zones are unaffected: `instance(0)` still returns the UTC singleton, `parseSpecifier("UTC+6")`/`"UTC-6:00"`, numeric offsets and "UTC+1"/"UTC" strings all remain valid. Full suite: same 892 passing, only the 2 pre-existing ICU/locale failures remain; eslint clean.
